principle: Begin with the viewer's question, observed material and narrative beat. Choose one focal event. These are editable craft patterns, not beauty scores or trained visual understanding.

cards.question: Where are we in the story, and what changes next?
cards.build: A large active chapter/date, readable named stages and a controlled progression. Reveal hierarchy before detail; keep the same spatial positions through successive stages.
cards.avoid: Thin full-width timelines whose labels are unreadable on a phone; giving every stage equal emphasis while discussing only one.

cards.question: How large is this quantity, and compared with what?
cards.build: One dominant number with its unit, a bounded 0–100 share bar when a real percentage is supplied, then a concise interpretation and visible source. Show the baseline before the difference.
cards.avoid: Decorative counters, misleading bar baselines, invented equivalents or precision not present in the source.

cards.question: What does the claim say, and what does the dated record establish?
cards.build: Two readable records with explicit dates/sources; reveal the second after the first has had reading time. Keep evidence, narrator interpretation and reconstructed illustration distinct.
cards.avoid: Two walls of text; suggesting contradiction merely by placing unrelated statements side by side.

cards.question: Which words in the document support this sentence?
cards.build: Show the document first, move to the relevant passage, underline a short quotation as the voice reaches it, then return to the wider context.
cards.avoid: Unreadable full-page documents or typing an unattributed paraphrase as if it were an original quotation.

cards.question: Why does this route, terrain or distance matter?
cards.build: Orient on a readable map; identify two locations, reveal the route or obstacle at the spoken event, then resolve on evidence footage. Use prepared Blender terrain only when relief explains the event.
cards.avoid: Unmotivated globe spins, camera moves before labels are readable, unmarked historical reconstruction.

cards.question: Who experienced the change, and what concrete detail carries it?
cards.build: Begin with an observed face, hand, object or named personal account. A restrained tracked focus or depth move should direct attention to that detail, then connect the person back to the wider event.
cards.avoid: Anonymous stock footage presented as a named historical person; depth effects on every photograph.

cards.question: What decision changed which outcome?
cards.build: Present the initial condition, reveal the decision on its own beat, then reveal the supported outcome. Use a simple causal diagram or matched before/after evidence; label uncertainty.
cards.avoid: Arrows implying causation that the sources only describe as correlation.

cards.question: What should the viewer feel or reconsider after this event?
cards.build: Vary shot duration around meaning: compression into an event, a held consequence, then a motivated sound or visual bridge. Listen to the actual mix before placing a pause.
cards.avoid: Cutting every beat to music, treating long shots as automatically bad, constant cinematic impacts.

cards.question: Can the next place or event be heard before it is seen?
cards.build: Use sourced ambience/dialogue as a short J-cut; enter the image when the new sound has established location. Preserve the narrator's intelligibility and allow the source sound to resolve.
cards.avoid: Generic whooshes at every cut, fabricated archival sound presented as original.

cards.question: Where is attention at the end of this shot, and where should it land in the next?
cards.build: Inspect frames either side of a cut, match the subject or direction of motion, then choose the next crop. Use tracking coordinates in their actual source-to-canvas mapping.
cards.avoid: Choosing a transition from its name without checking both moving shots.

cards.question: What happened simultaneously in two places or accounts?
cards.build: Establish each strand separately, keep distinct date/place labels, then bring them into a controlled split-screen or alternating sequence. Resolve on the consequence shared by the strands.
cards.avoid: A permanent split-screen that makes both records too small or suggests false simultaneity.

cards.question: What has changed when the opening person, object or image returns?
cards.build: Record the opening image and its meaning. Return to a verified related image with a changed context, framing or sound; let the difference complete the opening question.
cards.avoid: Repeating a decorative logo or the same footage without a change in meaning.
